title: Template-free exponential amplification of arbitrary peptides

concept.text: Millennium Problems for Biology 10, Protein amplification chain reaction. Target: in a single pot, exponentially amplify arbitrary peptides into full-length, sequence-faithful copies from amino-acid monomers without a nucleic-acid template; at least 1000-fold increase in abundance with at least 90% per-residue accuracy, without explicit sequencing or reverse translation. Sources given: https://millenniumproblems.bio/.

change_log.change: Added by hand to BCH on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the twelve Millennium Problems for Biology (Sam Rodriques and Michaela Hinks, FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, 2026), each with a stated concrete target; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Protein amplification chain reaction
page.definition: An input peptide, a chain of amino acids, directs the formation of full-length copies of its sequence from individual amino acids in one reaction mixture. The copies direct further copying, so their number grows exponentially. The reaction must work on arbitrary sequences without first reading the sequence, encoding it in DNA or RNA, or supplying a matching scaffold. In a laboratory demonstration with a short peptide, the product helped add one amino acid to a chain already one residue short of completion.

goal.need: A single mammalian cell contains about 100–500 picograms of protein in total. Losses during preparation leave still less for mass spectrometry, so scarce proteins can escape identification. More sensitive detectors make better use of the molecules available. Copying a surviving peptide would supply more molecules carrying its sequence for measurement, helping investigators identify proteins that distinguish cell states or serve as disease biomarkers. That benefit depends on at least one original molecule reaching the copying reaction.

statements.quote: Demonstrate exponential amplification of arbitrary peptide substrates.

statements.body: Marcotte laboratory, University of Texas at Austin
statements.quote: Unlike the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for nucleic acids, no methods exist for template-directed amplification of proteins.
statements.context: The protein-sequencing developers identify this limitation while motivating methods for measuring individual peptide molecules.

completion.title: A pool of ≥100 random peptides is amplified ≥1,000-fold with ≥90% accuracy per residue.
completion.criterion: Preregister, synthesize and pool at least 100 random peptide sequences of at least 50 residues each. Show exponential growth in peptide abundance in solution by at least 1,000-fold, with at least 90% sequence accuracy per residue. The input peptides must direct one-pot synthesis of new, full-length covalent copies from amino-acid monomers. Exclude nucleic-acid templates, preformed matching scaffolds, explicit sequencing as a copying step and reverse translation through nucleic acids. Reasonable modifications for post-amplification analysis are permitted if inactive during amplification.
completion.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, Millennium Problems for Biology, problem 10.
completion.threshold_quote: It must then be shown that the abundance of these peptides in solution can be amplified at least 1000x with at least 90% sequence accuracy on a per-residue basis.
completion.basis: Problem 10 specifies the acceptance conditions. In September 2026, Sam Rodriques announced that FutureHouse would convene a panel to judge success.

milestones.title: A peptide accelerates formation of covalent copies of itself from peptide fragments.
milestones.criterion: Compare reactions containing the same shorter peptide fragments and different starting amounts of the full-length product, including a reaction with no added product. Increasing the starting amount of product must increase the initial rate at which the fragments join to form new covalent copies of that peptide.
milestones.set_by: Chemical self-replication convention, applied by Ghadiri's group in Nature (1996); the published demonstration concerns a designed helical peptide.
milestones.threshold_quote: Marked increases in the initial rates of product (template) formation are observed as the initial concentration of the template is increased.

milestones.title: A peptide-based chemical replicator exhibits first-order replication kinetics.
milestones.criterion: At effectively constant precursor concentration, the rate at which a peptide-based replicator forms new copies must be proportional to its own concentration. The reaction order with respect to the replicator is 1.
milestones.set_by: Chemical self-replication convention, explicitly stated by Colomb-Delsuc and colleagues in Nature Communications (2015); their experiment concerns peptide-functionalized macrocycles.
milestones.threshold_quote: Exponential growth occurs only when the order in autocatalyst is 1.

milestones.title: A peptide template directs three sequence-selective amino-acid additions.
milestones.criterion: Starting with a five-residue peptide and a mixture containing both mirror-image forms of arginine and phenylalanine, identify the eight-residue product with the specified alternating sequence and all-L stereochemistry. Compare reactions with and without the complementary peptide template to establish that formation of this triple-addition product depends on the template.
milestones.set_by: Rout, Friedmann, Riek and Greenwald, Nature Communications (2018), experimental benchmark for alternating amyloid-forming peptides.
milestones.threshold_quote: 1 of 64 possible triple addition products, under conditions in which the absence of template yields only single and double additions of mixed stereochemistry.

milestones.title: A pool of ≥100 random peptides is copied exponentially with ≥90% per-residue accuracy.
milestones.criterion: Meet the completion conditions for the pooled random peptides, including full-length copying, exponential growth in solution and at least 90% sequence accuracy per residue. At this intermediate stage any demonstrated exponential gain qualifies, including a gain below 1,000-fold.
milestones.set_by: Atlas. No external body specifies a penultimate gain threshold for this challenge.

milestones.title: A peptide promotes formation of its own sequence by one stereoselective amino-acid addition.
milestones.criterion: Supply a peptide one residue short of the target and both mirror-image forms of the missing amino acid. Compare reactions with and without added target peptide. After subtracting the amount added, the seeded reaction must give a higher yield of newly formed target and a higher ratio of target to product bearing the opposite stereochemistry at the added residue.
milestones.set_by: Rout, Rhyner, Riek and Greenwald, product-seeding comparison in Figure 1D.
milestones.threshold_quote: act as self-replicators to enhance the yield and stereoselectivity of their formation.

not_found: Searches found no externally specified penultimate criterion for monomer-fed amplification of arbitrary peptide sequences.
No published demonstration satisfying completion or the Atlas penultimate test was found through 14 November 2026.
The challenge does not specify a kinetic fitting rule, a random-sequence sampling scheme, or whether gain and accuracy thresholds apply separately to each sequence or to pooled averages.
No statement from a scientific society or challenge programme disputing the value or feasibility of problem 10 was found.

results.finding: Peptide-functionalized disulfide hexamers accumulated faster at higher seed levels across four conditions, with 3–4 measurements per level.
results.detail: The matched series used 5–20 mol% hexamer seed. The separately reported unseeded time course started from building block 1 and ran at 1,500 rpm, whereas the seeded series used a partially oxidized library at 1,200 rpm.

results.finding: Peptide-functionalized hexamer fibres showed replication order 0.996 ± 0.166 (SD) across four seed levels, with 3–4 measurements per level.
results.detail: The experimental uncertainty alone leaves room for sub-exponential growth. The measured fibre-length behavior and the model with fibre breakage provide additional support for first-order kinetics.
